messages:
irene: Heads up — planning to provision a new GPU nodepool in us-east4 to serve low-latency infer for east-coast customers. Need input on instance types, sizing, and any IP/quota gotchas.

sanjay: What's the target qps and typical pod request/limit for the workloads? bursty or steady?

irene: Mostly bursty realtime v1 endpoints (p50 ~ 30ms target). Expect peaks ~1200 rps, steady ~200. Pods request 4g GPUs or shareable embeddings pods 0.25 GPU.

alex: For that profile i'd consider a mixed pool: a10g for most traffic (cheaper, good perf for quantized models) + a small H100 subpool for long-context / larger models. Keep embeddings on a10g.

marie: Agree on mixed. Two operational notes: (1) us-east4 subnet IPs are tight in our project right now — watch secondary range size for node pools, (2) NAT egress capacity matters if we create many nodes in multi-az.

marie: Quick example gcloud nodepool command we use as a template:
```
# create a10g pool with taint and autoscaler
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-a10g-pool \
  --cluster=redwood-prod-cluster \
  --zone=us-east4-b \
  --machine-type=n2-standard-32 \
  --accelerator=type=a100,count=1 \
  --num-nodes=2 --min-nodes=2 --max-nodes=12 \
  --node-labels=instance-type=a10g,gpu=true \
  --node-taints=gpu=true:NoSchedule \
  --enable-autoscaling
```
(adjust machine-type/accelerator field for H100 pool)

dev_ops_bot: Quota snapshot for project: GPUs remaining: 68, vCPUs remaining: 520, subnet secondary IPs available: 36.

alex: 36 IPs might be the blocker — if each node consumes an IP and we plan autoscale to 12 nodes per AZ it's tight. Two options: increase secondary range size or enable alias IP + larger range.

sanjay: Also think about cluster-autoscaler pod priority config: prefer pre-scaling a10g pool since those are cheaper; use PodPriority + nodeSelector so critical realtime pods land on non-preemptible nodes.

irene: What about preemptible/spot for a10g? saves cost but worried about p99 spikes.

alex: Use mixed policy: make default a10g nodes preemptible to handle background/fill traffic and keep a small non-preemptible reserved set (e.g., min 2-4 nodes) for steady critical routing. Configure pod disruption budgets and checkpointing for stateful tasks.

marie: Also recommend taint based eviction: label reserve nodes as gpu=reserved and use tolerations only on critical priority class. That avoids noisy neighbor reclaim during scale-down.

ops-oncall: I can open a GCP quota increase for GPUs and secondary IPs. Need justification and target numbers. What should I request?

irene: Request +200 GPUs in us-east4, +1200 vCPUs, and bump subnet secondary IP range to 256 addresses. Mention low-latency product launch + perf testing for CAAS.

ops-oncall: Filing now — case template: 
"Project: redwood-prod. Region: us-east4. Increase quotas for GPUs (NVIDIA A10G equivalent) to 200 total, CPUs to 1200, and secondary IP range for subnet redwood-us-east4-secondary to /24. Usage: production inference serving for low-latency customers; autoscaling expected; provide current utilization charts."

dev_ops_bot: Support case created: CASE-2026-1197. GCP replied: initial review required, expect 48-72h.

marie: For rollout plan: start with a10g pool in single AZ with min 3 nodes (2 reserved non-preemptible + 1 preemptible), autoscale max 20. Add H100 pool (min 0 max 4) with nodeAffinity for heavy-model jobs. Test egress/NAT throughput before multi-AZ.

alex: Also set cluster-autoscaler balance-similar-node-groups=false for mixed pools, and tune scaleDownUtilizationThresholds so the H100 pool isn't aggressively scaled down while jobs are in flight.

irene: Perfect. I'll proceed once quota increase is in. Can someone add the terraform snippets to the infra PR? cc @marie @alex

marie: I'll prepare TF module and include scripted checks for subnet secondary range and a preflight that fails if IPs < required.

alex: :thumbsup:

sanjay: one more — add CI check that deploys a canary load to the new pool to validate p50/p95 before DNS cutover.

irene: Yep. Thanks all — follow-ups in this thread.
